## Skills
A skill is a set of instructions provided through a `SKILL.md` source. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and source locator. `file` locators are on the host filesystem, `environment resource` locators are owned by an execution environment, `orchestrator resource` locators are opaque non-filesystem resources, and `custom resource` locators use their provider's access mechanism.

- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. issue.title: refactor: track architecture review findings across runtime and tooling
issue.body:
## Outcome

Turn the 2026-08-07 architecture review into owned implementation work without duplicating the existing roadmap. Each finding should either be routed to an existing issue, receive a focused successor issue, or be explicitly deferred with evidence.

The desired end state is less cross-module policy duplication, shorter validation feedback, deeper runtime-neutral operations, simpler runtime/test internals, and a more navigable repository control plane.

## Review baseline

- Repository snapshot: `origin/main` at `2443cad60f74c21ec38592d2083e7fac1398401a`.
- Exact local PR lane: `mise exec -- npm run test:pr -- --outputStyle=stream`.
- Cold run: **62.1s**; warm run: **33.0s**.
- The cold Nx report attributed **33.8s / 55%** to recoverable work; the warm report still attributed **13.8s / 43%**.
- `test:unit` selected 76 files / 842 tests. The contract, stdio, and CLI lanes added 13 file executions whose files were already selected by unit.
- The review was read-only: the source checkout and dedicated review worktree remained clean.

## Findings and current ownership

| # | Finding | Strength | Current owner / review delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One runtime-neutral endpoint policy module | **Strong — top recommendation** | Adjacent to #928, but not owned there as a cross-runtime source for retry semantics, expected 404s, safe diagnostics, and metric endpoint identity. Keep #928 responsible for failure reporting and telemetry ownership. |
| 2 | Complete the shared Hevy operations module | **Strong** | Continue #872. The workspace currently shares `workouts.list`; Core and CLI still independently implement other pagination, read, mutation, search, and aggregation workflows. |
| 3 | Make PR validation artifact-aware and disjoint | **Strong** | Continue #882 with the measured baseline above. Unit overlaps focused lanes, and package/performance paths rebuild artifacts already produced earlier in the graph. |
| 4 | Collapse Node lifecycle into one runner | **Strong** | Continue #878. The stdio and HTTP paths still repeat process tracking, cancellation, config, run spans, update scheduling, shutdown, telemetry flush, and failure classification. |
| 5 | Deepen deterministic MCP test support | **Strong** | Reassess #606, which is closed as `not_planned`. The two mocked integration suites still repeat server/client/runtime registration, in-memory transport, network isolation, and teardown; Core tool tests also repeat registration/handler discovery. |
| 6 | Compile and partition response contracts | **Worth exploring** | No direct issue found; #874 is adjacent but owns public MCP contract projection, not this private implementation. `response-contracts.ts` is 1,252 lines, constructs a Zod object during each render, and repeats pagination mechanics. Benchmark before claiming material runtime gain. |
| 7 | Measure Worker request admission before caching | **Speculative** | Continue #879. Every Worker POST currently performs an upstream `/v1/user/info` validation and creates/connects a new server and transport. Add a repeated-request Worker benchmark before considering any bounded reuse. |
| 8 | Deepen the repository control plane | **Worth exploring** | #873 is complete and #882 is adjacent, but residual duplication remains across control-plane validation, lane rendering, Nx metadata, selectors, and handwritten docs. Current onboarding still says five workspaces instead of six and references deleted paths. |

## Evidence by finding

### 1. Endpoint policy duplication

Relevant files:

- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/hevy-error-policy.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.ts`
- `packages/node/src/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts`
- `packages/operations/src/workouts.ts`

Endpoint identity and policy are represented by independent lists or branches. A change can therefore drift between client retry behavior, Core read-miss handling, safe diagnostics, operations behavior, and Node metric normalization.

The central model must keep distinct policy facts rather than flattening them into one broad allowlist. Unknown endpoints must remain fail-closed, and diagnostic redaction must not be weakened.

### 2. Shared operations remain shallow

Relevant files:

- `packages/operations/src/workouts.ts`
- `packages/operations/src/index.ts`
- `packages/core/src/tools/*.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts`

The operations workspace proves the desired seam through `workouts.list`, but most Core tools and CLI commands still orchestrate the curated Hevy client separately. Grow #872 domain by domain; adapters should retain argument parsing, presentation, and runtime observation rather than Hevy-domain workflow policy.

### 3. Validation repeats tests and builds

Relevant files:

- `project.json`
- `nx.json`
- `package.json`
- `repository/validation-lanes.json`
- `tests/package/*`
- `.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml`

Specialized contract, stdio, and CLI tests are all selected by unit and then executed again by their named lanes. The build/pack path also rebuilds Node and CLI artifacts inside package smoke work after earlier graph producers have run.

Disjointness must preserve complete coverage and focused debugging commands. Artifact consumers must reject stale output; this is not permission to remove custom policy checks or package-install smoke behavior.

### 4. Node lifecycle duplication

Relevant files:

- `packages/node/src/index.ts`
- `packages/node/src/utils/graceful-shutdown.ts`
- `packages/node/src/streamable-http.ts`
- `packages/node/src/index.test.ts`

`runStdioServer` and the HTTP runner repeat one substantial lifecycle implementation. A private lifecycle runner with two real transport adapters would improve locality without erasing transport-specific behavior.

### 5. Repeated deterministic test machinery

Relevant files:

- `tests/integration/mocked/hevy-mcp.mocked.integration.test.ts`
- `tests/integration/mocked/get-workout-count-events-mocked.integration.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/tools/*.test.ts`
- `docs/testing-strategy.md`

This is renewed current-state evidence for #606. A shared test-support module should remain private, fail on leaked sessions/interceptors/network calls, and preserve visible failure diagnostics.

### 6. Response-contract implementation breadth

Relevant files:

- `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.ts`
- `packages/core/src/utils/response-contracts.test.ts`

Keep the existing deep public response interface. Explore compiling each validation schema once and organizing private domain implementations around shared pagination behavior. Preserve exact structured schemas and legacy text output.

### 7. Unmeasured Worker admission cost

Relevant files:

- `packages/worker/src/worker.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/worker.test.ts`
- `tests/performance/scenario.ts`
- `tests/performance/performance.test.ts`

The first deliverable is a representative repeated-request benchmark. Any reuse design must explicitly preserve credential revocation, tenant isolation, request isolation, and stateless transport semantics.

### 8. Residual control-plane drift

Relevant files:

- `scripts/control-plane-validation.mjs`
- `scripts/control-plane-models.mjs`
- `scripts/repository-control-plane.mjs`
- `scripts/render-validation-lanes.mjs`
- `repository/validation-lanes.json`
- `project.json`
- `docs/contributor-onboarding.md`
- `docs/testing-strategy.md`

`control-plane-validation.mjs` is 1,091 lines. Twenty-six of 28 mapped lanes repeat the same alias and Nx target name. Validation/rendering code rereads overlapping sources, while handwritten changing facts have drifted.

Derive simple one-to-one projections from one validated model seam. Preserve custom commands, cache exceptions, runtime/package policy, release policy, and the compiler-backed dependency checker as explicit policy.

## Recommended routing order

1. Define the endpoint-policy ownership and coordinate it with #928.
2. Add the measured validation baseline and artifact-flow slice to #882.
3. Decide whether to reopen #606 or file a narrowed successor.
4. Continue shared operations through #872 and Node lifecycle through #878.
5. File a focused response-contract implementation/benchmark issue if accepted.
6. Add the Worker benchmark requirement to #879 before any reuse design.
7. Route residual control-plane and documentation drift to #882 or a focused successor.

This is an ordering for maintainer leverage, not a requirement to combine the work into one branch or pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every finding above is marked accepted, deferred, or rejected with a short rationale.
- [ ] Every accepted finding has exactly one owning issue; existing issues are reused where their scope already matches.
- [ ] The endpoint-policy owner distinguishes retry, expected-absence, diagnostic-safety, and metric-identity facts and remains fail-closed for unknown endpoints.
- [ ] #882 records the cold/warm baseline and requires before/after execution counts and wall time without weakening validation.
- [ ] #606 is either reopened, replaced by a narrower issue, or remains closed with a current rationale that addresses the repeated setup still present.
- [ ] Response-contract work is preceded by an allocation/render benchmark and preserves externally visible contracts.
- [ ] #879 receives a repeated-request Worker benchmark before any validation or server reuse is approved.
- [ ] Residual control-plane/docs drift has an owner and generated/parity-checked projections replace only derivable duplication.
- [ ] Accepted runtime/package changes identify their Changeset cascade from `repository/topology.json`.
- [ ] No accepted item requires editing `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/` by hand.

## Guardrails

- Preserve runtime-neutral direction: `hevy-client → operations → core`, with Node, Worker, and CLI as independent adapters.
- Keep generated client internals private and regenerated from their source.
- Keep npm scripts as compatibility entrypoints while Nx owns graph/input/output/cache metadata.
- Preserve the custom compiler-backed package-policy check; generic tooling may complement but not silently replace it.
- Do not broaden safe diagnostic data while deduplicating endpoint/error policy.
- Do not add Worker credential caching or shared mutable state without revocation and isolation evidence.
- Do not turn this tracking issue into one large implementation pull request.

## Validation expectations

Each implementation issue should run the focused lane for its changed seam plus the repository baseline:

```text
mise exec -- npm run check
mise exec -- npm run check:types
mise exec -- npm run build
mise exec -- npm run test:pr
mise exec -- npm run test:performance
mise exec -- npm run check:changeset
```

Performance-oriented work must publish the exact before/after command, cold/warm state, execution count, wall time, and any correctness trade-off.

## Non-goals

- Reopening completed roadmap issues merely to duplicate their accepted scope.
- Creating a second operations, lifecycle, Worker-routing, or validation model beside #872, #878, #879, or #882.
- Removing safety, release, package, privacy, or compatibility checks to improve timing.
- Designing a Worker cache before measuring the actual hot path.
- Splitting cohesive modules only because they are large.

## Review relationship

This is a current-checkout follow-up to the completed synthesis in #865 and portfolio decision in #866. It records what remains observable after subsequent architecture and Nx work, and routes those deltas into the live backlog.

issues.body:
## Primary changes
- compact all 25 MCP tool descriptions and input schemas while retaining direct tools and mutation safety
- normalize structured output sparsely and add compact workout/routine list projections
- add component token diagnostics, an enforced 8,900-token budget, and schema-version-2 baseline
- update integration contracts, documentation, and major-release changeset

## Reviewer walkthrough
- Review `packages/core/src/tools/` and `packages/core/src/tools/input-schemas.ts` for the compact tool catalog, input contracts, and retained direct tools.
- Review `packages/core/src/utils/response-formatter.ts` for sparse structured output normalization and compact workout/routine list projections.
- Review `scripts/measure-token-cost.ts`, `token-cost-baseline.json`, `.github/workflows/token-cost.yml`, and `docs/token-cost-tracking.md` for component diagnostics, the schema-version-2 baseline, and budget enforcement.
- Review the updated unit and integration contracts for coverage of the compact metadata and output behavior.

## Correctness and invariants
- Mutation safety remains in place while tool descriptions and input schemas are compacted.
- Structured output remains sparse, with compact projections for workout and routine lists.
- The token-cost baseline is schema version 2 and the enforced budget is 8,900 tokens.
- The 20-tool target remains advisory; all 25 direct tools are intentionally retained.

## Testing and QA
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run test:unit` (721 passed)
- `npm run test:mcp` (16 passed)
- `npm run measure:tokens -- --enforce-budget --baseline token-cost-baseline.json` (8,738 tokens)
- `npm run check:changeset`

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added `replace-workout-exercises` for explicit exercise replacement.
  * Token-cost measurement now supports an enforceable total budget gate (`--enforce-budget`) and enriched reporting.
  * Added `get-training-summary` to the MCP read-tool set.
* **Improvements**
  * MCP tools and CLI now consistently use `snake_case` request/response fields.
  * Responses are more compact: omitted optional/null fields and safer pagination behavior.
  * Stricter validation for identifiers, dates, and mutation/unknown-key handling.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated README and CLI docs to match the new tool names and `snake_case` contracts/prompts.

arguments.title: architecture: adopt a deep operations kernel with independent runtime hosts
arguments.body:
## Decision to review

Adopt **one deep runtime-neutral application spine with three honest runtime hosts**:

- deepen `@hevy-mcp/operations` into the application kernel shared by MCP and CLI callers;
- keep `@hevy-mcp/core` as the MCP projection of those operations;
- keep Node stdio, stateful Node HTTP, and stateless Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth as independent concrete adapters;
- share safe semantic observations, while leaving exporters and lifecycle behavior in the runtime adapters;
- do **not** introduce a universal Node/Worker base class.

This issue owns the cross-runtime architecture decision and its invariants. It does not replace the implementation issues already accepted in the roadmap.

## Review baseline

Repository snapshot: `origin/main` at `2443cad60f74c21ec38592d2083e7fac1398401a` on 2026-08-07.

The current macro-shape is sound, but the application seam is still shallow:

- `packages/operations` has about 131 production lines and shares only `workouts.list`;
- Core has roughly 5,978 production lines and still contains 13 direct `runtime.getClient()` call sites versus one `runtime.getOperations()` call;
- execution scoping relies on a hand-maintained client option-index table and proxy;
- Node has rich tool, cache, client, and telemetry observation wiring, while the Worker does not yet project the same safe semantic events;
- Node HTTP sessions and isolated Worker requests have materially different state and lifecycle semantics.

## Target ownership

| Module | Owns | Must not own |
|---|---|---|
| `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | upstream HTTP mechanics, curated generated-client edge, endpoint identity, retry/request phases | MCP presentation, CLI rendering, runtime lifecycle |
| `@hevy-mcp/operations` | Hevy intents, pagination/search/composites, mutation safety, normalized outcomes, safe semantic observations | MCP schemas, process signals, Cloudflare bindings |
| `@hevy-mcp/core` | MCP tools/prompts/resources, response contracts, tool execution and protocol projection | Node process lifecycle, Worker auth/routing |
| `hevy-mcp` Node adapter | stdio, stateful HTTP sessions, shutdown, process/update lifecycle, Node exporters | Worker request semantics |
| `@hevy-mcp/worker` | request admission, bearer/OAuth routing, origin/CORS, request isolation, Cloudflare bindings/export | Node session/process abstractions |
| CLI adapter | argument parsing and human/JSON rendering | duplicate Hevy-domain workflows |

Dependency direction remains runtime-neutral: client mechanics feed operations, operations feed Core, and CLI consumes operations directly. Node and Worker compose Core independently.

## Runtime composition

### Node stdio

One process-scoped host composes a credential-scoped client, operations kernel, MCP projection, stdio transport, process lifecycle, and Node observation exporters.

### Node HTTP

One process host owns the HTTP listener and shutdown. Each stateful MCP session owns its server/transport and credential-scoped operation graph. Session security and cleanup stay concrete.

### Cloudflare Worker

Each admitted request remains isolated: authenticate, create a credential-scoped client/operations/Core graph, connect a stateless transport, respond, and dispose. Do not cache credential validation or mutable server state without the benchmark, revocation, and tenant-isolation evidence required by #879.

## Required invariants

- Adding a domain operation should not require a new execution-proxy index plus independent Core and CLI workflow implementations.
- Operation inputs and outcomes are concrete and typed; avoid a stringly `execute(capabilityId, unknown)` dispatcher.
- Expected absence, retryability, safe diagnostics, and metric identity remain distinct endpoint-policy facts. Unknown endpoints fail closed.
- Generated Kubb internals remain private behind curated Hevy client exports.
- Safe semantic observation is runtime-neutral; Sentry/OpenTelemetry/Cloudflare exporters remain adapter-specific.
- Node process/session state never leaks into the Worker, and Worker request isolation is not weakened for superficial reuse.
- MCP protocol compatibility is projected by Core and is not allowed to distort the application interface.
- No giant facade that merely mirrors every generated client method, and no capability megamanifest as a second source of truth.

## Migration route

Reuse the live roadmap instead of creating one large implementation branch:

1. Route the central endpoint-policy slice through #937 and coordinate its telemetry ownership with #928.
2. Deepen operations domain by domain in #872, starting with one end-to-end vertical slice.
3. Move explicit execution context and normalized outcomes with the operation slice; retire proxy-table entries only as callers migrate.
4. Keep public MCP contract work in #874 and the protocol-serving seam in #876.
5. Collapse duplicated Node lifecycle through #878 without merging stdio and HTTP transport implementations.
6. Add Worker semantic-observation parity and measure request admission through #879 before considering reuse.
7. Preserve the runtime contract matrix and isolation evidence in #880.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Maintainers mark this target architecture accepted, deferred, or rejected with rationale.
- [ ] The attached HTML review is commit-pinned and checksum-verified.
- [ ] A concrete operations interface is compared against at least two materially different designs before implementation.
- [ ] The first vertical slice has one owning implementation issue and explicit module ownership.
- [ ] Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker request lifecycles are covered by contract tests that preserve their different state models.
- [ ] Worker observation parity is measured semantically; runtime-specific exporter configuration is not forced into Core.
- [ ] Each implementation PR identifies its package/Changeset cascade from `repository/topology.json`.
- [ ] No implementation PR attempts to combine the full migration.

## Non-goals

- A universal runtime host or inheritance hierarchy.
- Combining stateful Node HTTP and stateless Worker transport code.
- Caching Worker credentials or mutable server state without evidence.
- Replacing curated, typed operations with a generic registry dispatcher.
- Duplicating #872, #874, #876, #878, #879, or #880.

## External constraints

The TypeScript SDK intentionally supports both stateful and stateless deployment modes: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/docs/server.md

Cloudflare recommends the stateless handler for new Worker servers: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/apis/handler-api/

## Relationship to prior review

#937 remains the broader architecture-improvement tracker. This issue records the narrower Node/Cloudflare target architecture and routes its implementation through the existing roadmap.

4. Keep public MCP contract work in #874 and the protocol-serving seam in #876.
5. Collapse duplicated Node lifecycle through #878 without merging stdio and HTTP transport implementations.
6. Add Worker semantic-observation parity and measure request admission through #879 before considering reuse.
7. Preserve the runtime contract matrix and isolation evidence in #880.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Maintainers mark this target architecture accepted, deferred, or rejected with rationale.
- [ ] The attached HTML review is commit-pinned and checksum-verified.
- [ ] A concrete operations interface is compared against at least two materially different designs before implementation.
- [ ] The first vertical slice has one owning implementation issue and explicit module ownership.
- [ ] Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker request lifecycles are covered by contract tests that preserve their different state models.
- [ ] Worker observation parity is measured semantically; runtime-specific exporter configuration is not forced into Core.
- [ ] Each implementation PR identifies its package/Changeset cascade from `repository/topology.json`.
- [ ] No implementation PR attempts to combine the full migration.

## Non-goals

- A universal runtime host or inheritance hierarchy.
- Combining stateful Node HTTP and stateless Worker transport code.
- Caching Worker credentials or mutable server state without evidence.
- Replacing curated, typed operations with a generic registry dispatcher.
- Duplicating #872, #874, #876, #878, #879, or #880.

## External constraints

The TypeScript SDK intentionally supports both stateful and stateless deployment modes: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/docs/server.md

Cloudflare recommends the stateless handler for new Worker servers: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/apis/handler-api/

## Relationship to prior review

#937 remains the broader architecture-improvement tracker. This issue records the narrower Node/Cloudflare target architecture and routes its implementation through the existing roadmap.

Architecture review Snapshot 2443cad 7 August 2026 Read-only

One deep application spine.
Three honest runtime hosts.

The repository already has the right macro-shape. The best architecture is to deepen the runtime-neutral operation and capability modules, then keep Node stdio, Node HTTP, and the Cloudflare Worker as independent adapters with their own lifecycle, authentication, and state.

Top recommendation

Finish the shared operations kernel; do not add a universal runtime base class.

The first bounded slice should centralize endpoint policy, then continue operations domain by domain.

Decision in one minute

Preserve the seams that are real

  • Deep shared modules: Hevy client mechanics, endpoint/execution policy, domain operations, capability semantics, and MCP projection.
  • Concrete adapters: Node stdio, stateful Node HTTP, stateless Worker HTTP/OAuth, and CLI presentation.
  • Shared semantic events: safe tool, cache, request, and outcome observations; exporters remain runtime-specific.
  • No transport unification: stateful sessions and process shutdown are not the same problem as isolated Worker requests.
This report deliberately stops before concrete TypeScript interface design. Candidate selection comes first.

Recommended target shape

Measured current state

The architecture is asymmetrically deep

Core is already deep and valuable. Operations is still a pilot. Runtime observation is rich on Node and coarse on Worker. Those asymmetries, not the package diagram itself, are the main sources of change amplification.

01

Complete the operations and capability kernel

Strongest

Turn the one-operation pilot into the application module that owns Hevy intent and policy across MCP and CLI.

  • Existing owner: issue #872.

Problem

Expected absence, pagination, search, mutation semantics, and composite workflows still live in presentation modules. The operations module is too shallow to justify its seam under the deletion test.

Direction

Migrate vertical domains incrementally. Operations owns intent-level normalization and outcomes; core owns MCP schemas and response presentation; CLI owns parsing and rendering. Delete superseded policy and tests as each slice lands.

Benefits

  • One policy owner for two real production adapters.

02

Create one endpoint-policy vocabulary

Best first slice

Centralize endpoint identity while keeping retry, absence, diagnostic safety, and metric identity as distinct facts.

Files and evidence

  • hevy-client-kubb.ts:137-186 — safe, expected-404, and dynamic endpoint lists.
  • core/utils/hevy-error-policy.ts:7-66 — overlapping read/list/mutation sets.
  • core/utils/error-policy.ts:99-149 — safe codes, endpoints, and source identities.
  • node/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts:19-45 — another endpoint normalizer.
  • Current routing owner: issue #937.

Problem

An endpoint change can drift among retry behavior, expected absence, privacy-safe diagnostics, operations behavior, and metric labels. A broad allowlist would be dangerous because those facts have different security and product meaning.

Direction

Give canonical endpoint identity one neutral owner and let each policy consume explicit facts. Unknown endpoints remain fail-closed. This is a bounded prerequisite for deepening operations and aligning observation.

Before → after

    ID --> D["Diagnostic facts"]
    ID --> M["Metric identity"]
  end

  class ID,R,N,D,M after

Benefits

  • High change leverage with a small first migration.
  • Stronger privacy because unknown identity stays explicit.
  • Removes one major source of cross-module drift.
  • Creates stable vocabulary for operations and both observation adapters.
03

Deepen each runtime host without merging them

Strong

Improve locality inside Node and Worker while keeping three concrete transport lifetimes.

Files and evidence

  • node/src/index.ts:303-497 — duplicated stdio/HTTP lifecycle policy.
  • node/utils/streamable-http.ts:231-494 — stateful sessions, admission, disconnect, cleanup.
  • worker/src/worker.ts:323-566 — stateless exchange plus raw-key/OAuth routing.
  • worker/src/worker-oauth.ts:328-540 — OAuth grant and authorized request path.
  • Existing owners: #878 Node, #879 Worker, #876 protocol serving.

Problem

Node repeats startup, telemetry, failure classification, cancellation, and shutdown between stdio and HTTP. Worker normalizes origin/config more than once across raw-key and OAuth branches. A cross-runtime base class would hide rather than solve these differences.

Direction

Use one private Node lifecycle owner around two transport adapters. Use one Worker request-normalization owner before two auth adapters and one authenticated MCP exchange. Share only the primitive factory and neutral outcome vocabulary.

Recommended ownership

  PF --> WR["Worker request owner"]

  A2 --> X

  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
  class PF shared

Guardrail

Do not make Node stateful sessions and Worker stateless requests implement one universal lifecycle. The official SDK and Cloudflare guidance explicitly support different deployment modes.

04

Close the Worker observation seam

Strong targeted move

Keep one safe semantic event vocabulary while projecting it through runtime-native sinks.

Files and evidence

  • core/src/observation.ts:53-127 — privacy-safe tool observation interface.
  • core/src/utils/cache.ts:10-32 — cache observation seam.
  • node/src/index.ts:264-277 — Node wires tool, cache, and client observers.
  • worker/src/worker.ts:220-244 — Worker passes only client logging.
  • cloudflare.config.ts:20-53 — platform observability is enabled.
  • Related owner: issue #928.

Problem

The Worker has request-level logs and platform traces, but no application-level tool, cache, retry, or Hevy-call correlation through the existing neutral interface. “No Worker observability” would be inaccurate; semantic parity is the gap.

Direction

Implement a Worker-native adapter over existing bounded observations. Keep Sentry and Node OTel packages out of the Worker graph. Exporters may differ; event meaning and privacy rules should not.

Before → after

  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
  class EV1,EV2 shared

Benefits

  • Cross-runtime operational parity without exporter coupling.
  • One privacy review surface for semantic fields.
  • Tool and upstream failures become correlatable on Worker.
05

Separate Node embedding from executable startup

Worth exploring

Make the published programmatic interface safe to import without installing global telemetry providers.

Files and evidence

  • node/src/index.ts:1-37 — telemetry import must execute first.
  • node/utils/telemetry.ts:107-217 — import-time Sentry/OTel global setup.
  • node/src/index.ts:293-301 — public builder performs a network validation probe.
  • node/README.md:184-199 — published embedding contract.
  • node/tsdown.config.ts:58-99 — library and CLI share the same source graph.

Problem

The public library entrypoint and executable composition share import-time telemetry. An embedding application can therefore acquire global providers and network behavior merely by using the builder. This weakens locality and makes the interface shallower than its documentation suggests.

Direction

Separate a side-effect-free embedding entry from the executable bootstrap. The executable explicitly initializes telemetry, environment config, update checks, and process lifecycle before running the chosen transport.

    LIB["side-effect-free library entry"] --> BUILD2["embedded server composition"]

  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff

  class LIB,BUILD2,EXE,INIT,RUN2 after

Why not first?

This materially improves the public Node interface, but it does not resolve the larger shared-policy duplication. Coordinate it with Node lifecycle work rather than creating a second runner.

06

Prove the seam with one runtime contract matrix

Required proof

Exercise the same primitive catalog and outcome semantics through core, Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker HTTP.

Files and evidence

  • tests/integration/mocked/* — broad core contract coverage.
  • tests/integration/worker-http.integration.test.ts:504-705 — representative Worker coverage.
  • node/utils/streamable-http.test.ts — stateful host behavior.
  • worker/src/worker.test.ts:383-440 — fresh server/transport per Worker request.
  • Existing owner: issue #880.

Problem

Adapter tests prove local mechanics, but parity of every primitive, schema, safe outcome, and protocol era is not yet one generated contract. A seam with three runtime adapters needs interface-level proof.

Direction

Generate behavior cases from accepted capability descriptors, execute them through each supported host, and keep host-specific lifecycle tests separate. Tests consume the model; they do not redefine it.

Proof topology

flowchart LR
  MODEL["Capability + outcome model"] --> MATRIX["Generated contract matrix"]
  MATRIX --> CORE["in-memory core"]
  MATRIX --> STDIO["Node stdio"]
  MATRIX --> HTTP["Node HTTP"]
  MATRIX --> WORKER["Worker HTTP"]
  CORE --> REPORT["Parity report"]
  STDIO --> REPORT
  HTTP --> REPORT
  WORKER --> REPORT
  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
  class MODEL,MATRIX,REPORT shared
  class CORE,STDIO,HTTP,WORKER adapter

Benefits

  • Runtime parity becomes executable, not documentary.
  • Protocol upgrades expose drift before deployment.
  • Deep modules can replace shallow tests with confidence.

Small vertical moves toward the target

Endpoint identity

One identity owner; distinct fail-closed policy facts.

Migrate reads, writes, search, then workflows; delete duplicates.

03

Project capabilities through one primitive factory.

Runtime hosts

Refactor Node and Worker independently around their real lifetimes.

Conformance matrix plus runtime-native observation.

Decision record and current guidance

Repository decisions

  • #865 architecture synthesis

  • #937 current-checkout review routing

Primary external guidance

  • MCP TypeScript SDK server guide — stateful/stateless deployment and host protection.
  • Cloudflare MCP handler guide — stateless Worker handler as the current default.

Method: current source inspection, deletion test, module depth, seam reality, change leverage, locality, adapter parity, live issue state, and current primary SDK/runtime guidance. No source or repository file was changed.

Three honest runtime hosts. +

+

+ The repository already has the right macro-shape. The best + architecture is to deepen the runtime-neutral operation and + capability modules, then keep Node stdio, Node HTTP, and the + Cloudflare Worker as independent adapters with their own + lifecycle, authentication, and state. +

+
+
+

+ Top recommendation +

+

+ Finish the shared operations kernel; do not add a universal + runtime base class. +

+

+ The first bounded slice should centralize endpoint policy, then + continue operations domain by domain. +

+
+
+
+ +
+
+

+ Decision in one minute +

+

+ Preserve the seams that are real +

+
    +
  • + Deep shared modules: + Hevy client mechanics, endpoint/execution policy, domain + operations, capability semantics, and MCP projection. +
    • +
  • + Concrete adapters: Node + stdio, stateful Node HTTP, stateless Worker HTTP/OAuth, and CLI + presentation. +
    • +
  • + Shared semantic events: + safe tool, cache, request, and outcome observations; exporters + remain runtime-specific. +
    • +
  • + No transport unification: + stateful sessions and process shutdown are not the same problem as + isolated Worker requests. +
    • +
+
+ This report deliberately stops before concrete TypeScript interface + design. Candidate selection comes first. +
+

+
+

+ Recommended target shape +

+ arrows = consumption +

+  HEVY["Hevy HTTP"] --> CLIENT["hevy-client\nrequest adapter"]
+  POLICY["Endpoint + execution\npolicy"] --> CLIENT
+  CLIENT --> OPS["Operations + capability\napplication kernel"]
+  OPS --> MCP["Core MCP projection\n+ primitive factory"]

+  MCP --> NHTTP["Node HTTP host\nstateful sessions"]

+  classDef neutral fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px

+  class CLIENT,POLICY,OPS,MCP,EVENTS neutral
+  class STDIO,NHTTP,WORKER,CLI,NOTEL,CF adapter

+
+

+ Boxes do not imply one package per box. Prefer ownership and + deletion leverage over package count. +

+
+
+ +
+
+
+

+ Measured current state +

+

+ The architecture is asymmetrically deep +

+

+ Core is already deep and valuable. Operations is still a pilot. + Runtime observation is rich on Node and coarse on Worker. Those + asymmetries, not the package diagram itself, are the main sources + of change amplification. +

+
+
+
+

+

+ Structural value before implementation convenience +

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +

2 + One endpoint-policy vocabulary + HighVery highVery highHigh + Best first slice +

+

+
+ +
+
+ 01 +

+ Complete the operations and capability kernel +

+ Strongest +
+

+ Turn the one-operation pilot into the application module that + owns Hevy intent and policy across MCP and CLI. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + packages/operations/src/index.ts:18-29 — only + workouts.list. +
    • +
  • + packages/operations/src/workouts.ts:10-101 — + the entire production implementation. +
    • +
  • + packages/core/src/tools/* — 13 direct client + call sites versus one operations call. +
    • +
  • + packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts:97-448 — + most orchestration still bypasses operations. +
    • +
  • + Existing owner: + issue #872. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ Expected absence, pagination, search, mutation semantics, and + composite workflows still live in presentation modules. The + operations module is too shallow to justify its seam under the + deletion test. +

+

Direction

+

+ Migrate vertical domains incrementally. Operations owns + intent-level normalization and outcomes; core owns MCP schemas + and response presentation; CLI owns parsing and rendering. + Delete superseded policy and tests as each slice lands. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph B["Before"]
+    BC["MCP core"] --> BCL["Hevy client"]
+    BCLI["CLI"] --> BCL
+    BOPS["operations\nworkouts.list only"] --> BCL
+    BC -. one call .-> BOPS
+  end
+  subgraph A["After"]
+    ACORE["MCP projection"] --> AOPS["Deep operations\n+ capability kernel"]
+    ACLI["CLI adapter"] --> AOPS
+    AOPS --> ACL["Hevy client"]
+  end
+  classDef before fill:#301d2a,stroke:#fb7185,color:#fff
+  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff

+  class ACORE,AOPS,ACLI,ACL after
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • One policy owner for two real production adapters.
    • +
  • + Core becomes a deeper MCP projection instead of a mixed + application module. +
    • +
  • + Operation-level tests replace duplicated tool/CLI + implementation tests. +
    • +
  • + Future runtime hosts reuse application behavior without + new transport abstractions. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 02 +

+ Create one endpoint-policy vocabulary +

+ Best first slice +
+

+ Centralize endpoint identity while keeping retry, absence, + diagnostic safety, and metric identity as distinct facts. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + hevy-client-kubb.ts:137-186 — safe, + expected-404, and dynamic endpoint lists. +
    • +
  • + core/utils/hevy-error-policy.ts:7-66 — + overlapping read/list/mutation sets. +
    • +
  • + core/utils/error-policy.ts:99-149 — safe codes, + endpoints, and source identities. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts:19-45 — + another endpoint normalizer. +
    • +
  • + Current routing owner: + issue #937. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ An endpoint change can drift among retry behavior, expected + absence, privacy-safe diagnostics, operations behavior, and + metric labels. A broad allowlist would be dangerous because + those facts have different security and product meaning. +

+

Direction

+

+ Give canonical endpoint identity one neutral owner and let + each policy consume explicit facts. Unknown endpoints remain + fail-closed. This is a bounded prerequisite for deepening + operations and aligning observation. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph B["Before: repeated registries"]
+    E1["client retry / expected 404"]
+    E2["core absence policy"]
+    E3["safe diagnostics"]
+    E4["Node metric normalization"]
+  end
+  subgraph A["After: one identity, distinct facts"]
+    ID["Canonical endpoint identity"] --> R["Retry facts"]
+    ID --> N["Absence facts"]
+    ID --> D["Diagnostic facts"]
+    ID --> M["Metric identity"]
+  end
+  classDef before fill:#301d2a,stroke:#fb7185,color:#fff
+  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  class E1,E2,E3,E4 before
+  class ID,R,N,D,M after
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • High change leverage with a small first migration.
    • +
  • + Stronger privacy because unknown identity stays explicit. +
    • +
  • Removes one major source of cross-module drift.
    • +
  • + Creates stable vocabulary for operations and both + observation adapters. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 03 +

+ Deepen each runtime host without merging them +

+ Strong +
+

+ Improve locality inside Node and Worker while keeping three + concrete transport lifetimes. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + node/src/index.ts:303-497 — duplicated + stdio/HTTP lifecycle policy. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/streamable-http.ts:231-494 — + stateful sessions, admission, disconnect, cleanup. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker.ts:323-566 — stateless + exchange plus raw-key/OAuth routing. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker-oauth.ts:328-540 — OAuth + grant and authorized request path. +
    • +
  • + Existing owners: + #878 Node, + #879 Worker, + #876 protocol serving. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ Node repeats startup, telemetry, failure classification, + cancellation, and shutdown between stdio and HTTP. Worker + normalizes origin/config more than once across raw-key and + OAuth branches. A cross-runtime base class would hide rather + than solve these differences. +

+

Direction

+

+ Use one private Node lifecycle owner around two transport + adapters. Use one Worker request-normalization owner before + two auth adapters and one authenticated MCP exchange. Share + only the primitive factory and neutral outcome vocabulary. +

+
+
+

Recommended ownership

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  PF["Shared MCP primitive factory"] --> NL["Node lifecycle owner"]
+  PF --> WR["Worker request owner"]
+  NL --> S["stdio adapter"]
+  NL --> H["stateful HTTP adapter"]
+  WR --> A1["OAuth adapter"]
+  WR --> A2["direct-key adapter\nself-hosted / transition"]
+  A1 --> X["stateless authenticated exchange"]
+  A2 --> X
+  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
+  class PF shared
+  class NL,WR,S,H,A1,A2,X adapter
+
+
+

Guardrail

+

+ Do not make Node stateful sessions and Worker stateless + requests implement one universal lifecycle. The official SDK + and Cloudflare guidance explicitly support different + deployment modes. +

+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 04 +

+ Close the Worker observation seam +

+ Strong targeted move +
+

+ Keep one safe semantic event vocabulary while projecting it + through runtime-native sinks. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + core/src/observation.ts:53-127 — privacy-safe + tool observation interface. +
    • +
  • + core/src/utils/cache.ts:10-32 — cache + observation seam. +
    • +
  • + node/src/index.ts:264-277 — Node wires tool, + cache, and client observers. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker.ts:220-244 — Worker passes + only client logging. +
    • +
  • + cloudflare.config.ts:20-53 — platform + observability is enabled. +
    • +
  • + Related owner: + issue #928. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ The Worker has request-level logs and platform traces, but no + application-level tool, cache, retry, or Hevy-call correlation + through the existing neutral interface. “No Worker + observability” would be inaccurate; semantic parity is the + gap. +

+

Direction

+

+ Implement a Worker-native adapter over existing bounded + observations. Keep Sentry and Node OTel packages out of the + Worker graph. Exporters may differ; event meaning and privacy + rules should not. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart LR
+  subgraph B["Before"]
+    EV1["safe core events"] --> NO["Node observer"]
+    NO --> OT["OTel / Sentry"]
+    WREQ["Worker request logs"] --> CF1["Cloudflare"]
+  end
+  subgraph A["After"]
+    EV2["same safe events"] --> NO2["Node observer"]
+    EV2 --> WO["Worker observer"]
+    NO2 --> OT2["OTel / Sentry"]
+    WO --> CF2["Cloudflare-native sink"]
+  end
+  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
+  class EV1,EV2 shared
+  class NO,OT,WREQ,CF1,NO2,WO,OT2,CF2 adapter
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • + Cross-runtime operational parity without exporter + coupling. +
    • +
  • One privacy review surface for semantic fields.
    • +
  • + Tool and upstream failures become correlatable on Worker. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 05 +

+ Separate Node embedding from executable startup +

+ Worth exploring +
+

+ Make the published programmatic interface safe to import without + installing global telemetry providers. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + node/src/index.ts:1-37 — telemetry import must + execute first. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/telemetry.ts:107-217 — import-time + Sentry/OTel global setup. +
    • +
  • + node/src/index.ts:293-301 — public builder + performs a network validation probe. +
    • +
  • + node/README.md:184-199 — published embedding + contract. +
    • +
  • + node/tsdown.config.ts:58-99 — library and CLI + share the same source graph. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ The public library entrypoint and executable composition share + import-time telemetry. An embedding application can therefore + acquire global providers and network behavior merely by using + the builder. This weakens locality and makes the interface + shallower than its documentation suggests. +

+

Direction

+

+ Separate a side-effect-free embedding entry from the + executable bootstrap. The executable explicitly initializes + telemetry, environment config, update checks, and process + lifecycle before running the chosen transport. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph B["Before"]
+    IMP["import hevy-mcp"] --> GLOBAL["global telemetry init"]
+    GLOBAL --> BUILD["createNodeMcpServer"]
+    GLOBAL --> RUN["run executable"]
+  end
+  subgraph A["After"]
+    LIB["side-effect-free library entry"] --> BUILD2["embedded server composition"]
+    EXE["executable entry"] --> INIT["telemetry + config + lifecycle"]
+    INIT --> RUN2["stdio / HTTP runner"]
+  end
+  classDef before fill:#301d2a,stroke:#fb7185,color:#fff
+  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  class IMP,GLOBAL,BUILD,RUN before
+  class LIB,BUILD2,EXE,INIT,RUN2 after
+
+
+

Why not first?

+

+ This materially improves the public Node interface, but it + does not resolve the larger shared-policy duplication. + Coordinate it with Node lifecycle work rather than creating + a second runner. +

+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 06 +

+ Prove the seam with one runtime contract matrix +

+ Required proof +
+

+ Exercise the same primitive catalog and outcome semantics + through core, Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker HTTP. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + tests/integration/mocked/* — broad core + contract coverage. +
    • +
  • + tests/integration/worker-http.integration.test.ts:504-705 + — representative Worker coverage. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/streamable-http.test.ts — stateful + host behavior. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker.test.ts:383-440 — fresh + server/transport per Worker request. +
    • +
  • + Existing owner: + issue #880. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ Adapter tests prove local mechanics, but parity of every + primitive, schema, safe outcome, and protocol era is not yet + one generated contract. A seam with three runtime adapters + needs interface-level proof. +

+

Direction

+

+ Generate behavior cases from accepted capability descriptors, + execute them through each supported host, and keep + host-specific lifecycle tests separate. Tests consume the + model; they do not redefine it. +

+
+
+

Proof topology

+ 
+flowchart LR
+  MODEL["Capability + outcome model"] --> MATRIX["Generated contract matrix"]
+  MATRIX --> CORE["in-memory core"]
+  MATRIX --> STDIO["Node stdio"]
+  MATRIX --> HTTP["Node HTTP"]
+  MATRIX --> WORKER["Worker HTTP"]
+  CORE --> REPORT["Parity report"]
+  STDIO --> REPORT
+  HTTP --> REPORT
+  WORKER --> REPORT
+  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
+  class MODEL,MATRIX,REPORT shared
+  class CORE,STDIO,HTTP,WORKER adapter
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • Runtime parity becomes executable, not documentary.
    • +
  • Protocol upgrades expose drift before deployment.
    • +
  • + Deep modules can replace shallow tests with confidence. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+

+ Recommended sequence +

+

+ Small vertical moves toward the target +

+
+
+

01

+

Endpoint identity

+

+ One identity owner; distinct fail-closed policy facts. +

+
+
+

02

+

Operations domains

+

+ Migrate reads, writes, search, then workflows; delete duplicates. +

+
+
+

03

+

MCP projection

+

+ Project capabilities through one primitive factory. +

+
+
+

04

+

Runtime hosts

+

+ Refactor Node and Worker independently around their real + lifetimes. +

+
+
+

05

+

Parity proof

+

+ Conformance matrix plus runtime-native observation. +

+
+
+
+ +
+

+ Decision record and current guidance +

+
+
+

Repository decisions

+
    +
  • + #865 architecture synthesis +
    • +
  • + #866 accepted portfolio +
    • +
  • + #937 current-checkout review routing +
    • +
+
+
+

Primary external guidance

+
    +
  • + MCP TypeScript SDK server guide + — stateful/stateless deployment and host protection. +
    • +
  • + Cloudflare MCP handler guide + — stateless Worker handler as the current default. +
    • +
+
+
+

+ Method: current source inspection, deletion test, module depth, seam + reality, change leverage, locality, adapter parity, live issue state, + and current primary SDK/runtime guidance. No source or repository file + was changed. +

+

structuredContent.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,1218 @@ + + + + + + hevy-mcp Runtime Architecture Review + + + + + +
+
+
+ Architecture review + Snapshot 2443cad + 7 August 2026 + Read-only +
+
+
+

+ One deep application spine.
Three honest runtime hosts. +

+

+ The repository already has the right macro-shape. The best + architecture is to deepen the runtime-neutral operation and + capability modules, then keep Node stdio, Node HTTP, and the + Cloudflare Worker as independent adapters with their own + lifecycle, authentication, and state. +

+
+
+

+ Top recommendation +

+

+ Finish the shared operations kernel; do not add a universal + runtime base class. +

+

+ The first bounded slice should centralize endpoint policy, then + continue operations domain by domain. +

+
+
+
+ +
+
+

+ Decision in one minute +

+

+ Preserve the seams that are real +

+
    +
  • + Deep shared modules: + Hevy client mechanics, endpoint/execution policy, domain + operations, capability semantics, and MCP projection. +
    • +
  • + Concrete adapters: Node + stdio, stateful Node HTTP, stateless Worker HTTP/OAuth, and CLI + presentation. +
    • +
  • + Shared semantic events: + safe tool, cache, request, and outcome observations; exporters + remain runtime-specific. +
    • +
  • + No transport unification: + stateful sessions and process shutdown are not the same problem as + isolated Worker requests. +
    • +
+
+ This report deliberately stops before concrete TypeScript interface + design. Candidate selection comes first. +
+
+ +
+
+

+ Recommended target shape +

+ arrows = consumption +
+ 
+flowchart LR
+  HEVY["Hevy HTTP"] --> CLIENT["hevy-client\nrequest adapter"]
+  POLICY["Endpoint + execution\npolicy"] --> CLIENT
+  CLIENT --> OPS["Operations + capability\napplication kernel"]
+  OPS --> MCP["Core MCP projection\n+ primitive factory"]
+  OPS --> CLI["CLI adapter"]
+  MCP --> STDIO["Node stdio host"]
+  MCP --> NHTTP["Node HTTP host\nstateful sessions"]
+  MCP --> WORKER["Worker host\nstateless + OAuth"]
+  EVENTS["Safe observation\nvocabulary"] -.-> CLIENT
+  EVENTS -.-> OPS
+  EVENTS -.-> MCP
+  STDIO --> NOTEL["Node OTel / Sentry"]
+  NHTTP --> NOTEL
+  WORKER --> CF["Cloudflare logs / traces"]
+  classDef neutral fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff,stroke-width:2px
+  classDef external fill:#182635,stroke:#64748b,color:#fff
+  class CLIENT,POLICY,OPS,MCP,EVENTS neutral
+  class STDIO,NHTTP,WORKER,CLI,NOTEL,CF adapter
+  class HEVY external
+
+

+ Boxes do not imply one package per box. Prefer ownership and + deletion leverage over package count. +

+
+
+ +
+
+
+

+ Measured current state +

+

+ The architecture is asymmetrically deep +

+

+ Core is already deep and valuable. Operations is still a pilot. + Runtime observation is rich on Node and coarse on Worker. Those + asymmetries, not the package diagram itself, are the main sources + of change amplification. +

+
+
+
+

131

+

+ operations prod LOC +

+
+
+

5,978

+

+ core prod LOC +

+
+
+

13 : 1

+

+ core client : operations calls +

+
+
+

0

+

+ Worker observer hooks wired +

+
+
+
+
+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
ModuleCurrent depthDeletion testFinding
coreDeep + Removing it deletes the MCP contract for both runtimes. + + Keep and narrow it toward MCP projection. +
operationsShallow today + Removing it requires reverting one workout-list path. + + Deepen decisively or delete; two production adapters justify + the seam. +
nodeBroad + Removing it leaves Worker behavior intact. + + Improve locality inside the adapter; do not move process state + into core. +
workerBroad ingress + Removing it leaves Node behavior intact. + + Normalize routing/auth once, then project safe observations. +
+
+
+ +
+

+ Candidate ranking +

+

+ Structural value before implementation convenience +

+
+ + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
RankCandidateDepthLeverageLocalityRuntime parityRecommendation
1 + Complete operations + capabilities + Very highVery highHighHigh + Strongest structural move +
2 + One endpoint-policy vocabulary + HighVery highVery highHigh + Best first slice +
3 + Deepen each runtime host + HighHighVery highMedium + Strong, keep separate +
4 + Worker observation parity + HighMediumHighVery high + Strong targeted move +
5 + Side-effect-free Node embedding + HighMediumVery highLow + Worth exploring +
6 + Runtime contract matrix + MediumHighHighVery high + Required proof layer +
+
+
+ +
+
+ +
+
+ 01 +

+ Complete the operations and capability kernel +

+ Strongest +
+

+ Turn the one-operation pilot into the application module that + owns Hevy intent and policy across MCP and CLI. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + packages/operations/src/index.ts:18-29 — only + workouts.list. +
    • +
  • + packages/operations/src/workouts.ts:10-101 — + the entire production implementation. +
    • +
  • + packages/core/src/tools/* — 13 direct client + call sites versus one operations call. +
    • +
  • + packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts:97-448 — + most orchestration still bypasses operations. +
    • +
  • + Existing owner: + issue #872. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ Expected absence, pagination, search, mutation semantics, and + composite workflows still live in presentation modules. The + operations module is too shallow to justify its seam under the + deletion test. +

+

Direction

+

+ Migrate vertical domains incrementally. Operations owns + intent-level normalization and outcomes; core owns MCP schemas + and response presentation; CLI owns parsing and rendering. + Delete superseded policy and tests as each slice lands. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph B["Before"]
+    BC["MCP core"] --> BCL["Hevy client"]
+    BCLI["CLI"] --> BCL
+    BOPS["operations\nworkouts.list only"] --> BCL
+    BC -. one call .-> BOPS
+  end
+  subgraph A["After"]
+    ACORE["MCP projection"] --> AOPS["Deep operations\n+ capability kernel"]
+    ACLI["CLI adapter"] --> AOPS
+    AOPS --> ACL["Hevy client"]
+  end
+  classDef before fill:#301d2a,stroke:#fb7185,color:#fff
+  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  class BC,BCL,BCLI,BOPS before
+  class ACORE,AOPS,ACLI,ACL after
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • One policy owner for two real production adapters.
    • +
  • + Core becomes a deeper MCP projection instead of a mixed + application module. +
    • +
  • + Operation-level tests replace duplicated tool/CLI + implementation tests. +
    • +
  • + Future runtime hosts reuse application behavior without + new transport abstractions. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 02 +

+ Create one endpoint-policy vocabulary +

+ Best first slice +
+

+ Centralize endpoint identity while keeping retry, absence, + diagnostic safety, and metric identity as distinct facts. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + hevy-client-kubb.ts:137-186 — safe, + expected-404, and dynamic endpoint lists. +
    • +
  • + core/utils/hevy-error-policy.ts:7-66 — + overlapping read/list/mutation sets. +
    • +
  • + core/utils/error-policy.ts:99-149 — safe codes, + endpoints, and source identities. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts:19-45 — + another endpoint normalizer. +
    • +
  • + Current routing owner: + issue #937. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ An endpoint change can drift among retry behavior, expected + absence, privacy-safe diagnostics, operations behavior, and + metric labels. A broad allowlist would be dangerous because + those facts have different security and product meaning. +

+

Direction

+

+ Give canonical endpoint identity one neutral owner and let + each policy consume explicit facts. Unknown endpoints remain + fail-closed. This is a bounded prerequisite for deepening + operations and aligning observation. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph B["Before: repeated registries"]
+    E1["client retry / expected 404"]
+    E2["core absence policy"]
+    E3["safe diagnostics"]
+    E4["Node metric normalization"]
+  end
+  subgraph A["After: one identity, distinct facts"]
+    ID["Canonical endpoint identity"] --> R["Retry facts"]
+    ID --> N["Absence facts"]
+    ID --> D["Diagnostic facts"]
+    ID --> M["Metric identity"]
+  end
+  classDef before fill:#301d2a,stroke:#fb7185,color:#fff
+  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  class E1,E2,E3,E4 before
+  class ID,R,N,D,M after
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • High change leverage with a small first migration.
    • +
  • + Stronger privacy because unknown identity stays explicit. +
    • +
  • Removes one major source of cross-module drift.
    • +
  • + Creates stable vocabulary for operations and both + observation adapters. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 03 +

+ Deepen each runtime host without merging them +

+ Strong +
+

+ Improve locality inside Node and Worker while keeping three + concrete transport lifetimes. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + node/src/index.ts:303-497 — duplicated + stdio/HTTP lifecycle policy. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/streamable-http.ts:231-494 — + stateful sessions, admission, disconnect, cleanup. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker.ts:323-566 — stateless + exchange plus raw-key/OAuth routing. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker-oauth.ts:328-540 — OAuth + grant and authorized request path. +
    • +
  • + Existing owners: + #878 Node, + #879 Worker, + #876 protocol serving. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ Node repeats startup, telemetry, failure classification, + cancellation, and shutdown between stdio and HTTP. Worker + normalizes origin/config more than once across raw-key and + OAuth branches. A cross-runtime base class would hide rather + than solve these differences. +

+

Direction

+

+ Use one private Node lifecycle owner around two transport + adapters. Use one Worker request-normalization owner before + two auth adapters and one authenticated MCP exchange. Share + only the primitive factory and neutral outcome vocabulary. +

+
+
+

Recommended ownership

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  PF["Shared MCP primitive factory"] --> NL["Node lifecycle owner"]
+  PF --> WR["Worker request owner"]
+  NL --> S["stdio adapter"]
+  NL --> H["stateful HTTP adapter"]
+  WR --> A1["OAuth adapter"]
+  WR --> A2["direct-key adapter\nself-hosted / transition"]
+  A1 --> X["stateless authenticated exchange"]
+  A2 --> X
+  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
+  class PF shared
+  class NL,WR,S,H,A1,A2,X adapter
+
+
+

Guardrail

+

+ Do not make Node stateful sessions and Worker stateless + requests implement one universal lifecycle. The official SDK + and Cloudflare guidance explicitly support different + deployment modes. +

+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 04 +

+ Close the Worker observation seam +

+ Strong targeted move +
+

+ Keep one safe semantic event vocabulary while projecting it + through runtime-native sinks. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + core/src/observation.ts:53-127 — privacy-safe + tool observation interface. +
    • +
  • + core/src/utils/cache.ts:10-32 — cache + observation seam. +
    • +
  • + node/src/index.ts:264-277 — Node wires tool, + cache, and client observers. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker.ts:220-244 — Worker passes + only client logging. +
    • +
  • + cloudflare.config.ts:20-53 — platform + observability is enabled. +
    • +
  • + Related owner: + issue #928. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ The Worker has request-level logs and platform traces, but no + application-level tool, cache, retry, or Hevy-call correlation + through the existing neutral interface. “No Worker + observability” would be inaccurate; semantic parity is the + gap. +

+

Direction

+

+ Implement a Worker-native adapter over existing bounded + observations. Keep Sentry and Node OTel packages out of the + Worker graph. Exporters may differ; event meaning and privacy + rules should not. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart LR
+  subgraph B["Before"]
+    EV1["safe core events"] --> NO["Node observer"]
+    NO --> OT["OTel / Sentry"]
+    WREQ["Worker request logs"] --> CF1["Cloudflare"]
+  end
+  subgraph A["After"]
+    EV2["same safe events"] --> NO2["Node observer"]
+    EV2 --> WO["Worker observer"]
+    NO2 --> OT2["OTel / Sentry"]
+    WO --> CF2["Cloudflare-native sink"]
+  end
+  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
+  class EV1,EV2 shared
+  class NO,OT,WREQ,CF1,NO2,WO,OT2,CF2 adapter
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • + Cross-runtime operational parity without exporter + coupling. +
    • +
  • One privacy review surface for semantic fields.
    • +
  • + Tool and upstream failures become correlatable on Worker. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 05 +

+ Separate Node embedding from executable startup +

+ Worth exploring +
+

+ Make the published programmatic interface safe to import without + installing global telemetry providers. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + node/src/index.ts:1-37 — telemetry import must + execute first. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/telemetry.ts:107-217 — import-time + Sentry/OTel global setup. +
    • +
  • + node/src/index.ts:293-301 — public builder + performs a network validation probe. +
    • +
  • + node/README.md:184-199 — published embedding + contract. +
    • +
  • + node/tsdown.config.ts:58-99 — library and CLI + share the same source graph. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ The public library entrypoint and executable composition share + import-time telemetry. An embedding application can therefore + acquire global providers and network behavior merely by using + the builder. This weakens locality and makes the interface + shallower than its documentation suggests. +

+

Direction

+

+ Separate a side-effect-free embedding entry from the + executable bootstrap. The executable explicitly initializes + telemetry, environment config, update checks, and process + lifecycle before running the chosen transport. +

+
+
+

Before → after

+ 
+flowchart TB
+  subgraph B["Before"]
+    IMP["import hevy-mcp"] --> GLOBAL["global telemetry init"]
+    GLOBAL --> BUILD["createNodeMcpServer"]
+    GLOBAL --> RUN["run executable"]
+  end
+  subgraph A["After"]
+    LIB["side-effect-free library entry"] --> BUILD2["embedded server composition"]
+    EXE["executable entry"] --> INIT["telemetry + config + lifecycle"]
+    INIT --> RUN2["stdio / HTTP runner"]
+  end
+  classDef before fill:#301d2a,stroke:#fb7185,color:#fff
+  classDef after fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  class IMP,GLOBAL,BUILD,RUN before
+  class LIB,BUILD2,EXE,INIT,RUN2 after
+
+
+

Why not first?

+

+ This materially improves the public Node interface, but it + does not resolve the larger shared-policy duplication. + Coordinate it with Node lifecycle work rather than creating + a second runner. +

+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+ +
+
+ 06 +

+ Prove the seam with one runtime contract matrix +

+ Required proof +
+

+ Exercise the same primitive catalog and outcome semantics + through core, Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker HTTP. +

+
+ +
+
+
+

Files and evidence

+
    +
  • + tests/integration/mocked/* — broad core + contract coverage. +
    • +
  • + tests/integration/worker-http.integration.test.ts:504-705 + — representative Worker coverage. +
    • +
  • + node/utils/streamable-http.test.ts — stateful + host behavior. +
    • +
  • + worker/src/worker.test.ts:383-440 — fresh + server/transport per Worker request. +
    • +
  • + Existing owner: + issue #880. +
    • +
+

Problem

+

+ Adapter tests prove local mechanics, but parity of every + primitive, schema, safe outcome, and protocol era is not yet + one generated contract. A seam with three runtime adapters + needs interface-level proof. +

+

Direction

+

+ Generate behavior cases from accepted capability descriptors, + execute them through each supported host, and keep + host-specific lifecycle tests separate. Tests consume the + model; they do not redefine it. +

+
+
+

Proof topology

+ 
+flowchart LR
+  MODEL["Capability + outcome model"] --> MATRIX["Generated contract matrix"]
+  MATRIX --> CORE["in-memory core"]
+  MATRIX --> STDIO["Node stdio"]
+  MATRIX --> HTTP["Node HTTP"]
+  MATRIX --> WORKER["Worker HTTP"]
+  CORE --> REPORT["Parity report"]
+  STDIO --> REPORT
+  HTTP --> REPORT
+  WORKER --> REPORT
+  classDef shared fill:#123047,stroke:#3dd6d0,color:#fff
+  classDef adapter fill:#2a2038,stroke:#fbbf24,color:#fff
+  class MODEL,MATRIX,REPORT shared
+  class CORE,STDIO,HTTP,WORKER adapter
+
+
+

Benefits

+
    +
  • Runtime parity becomes executable, not documentary.
    • +
  • Protocol upgrades expose drift before deployment.
    • +
  • + Deep modules can replace shallow tests with confidence. +
    • +
+
+
+
+
+
+
+ +
+

+ Recommended sequence +

+

+ Small vertical moves toward the target +

+
+
+

01

+

Endpoint identity

+

+ One identity owner; distinct fail-closed policy facts. +

+
+
+

02

+

Operations domains

+

+ Migrate reads, writes, search, then workflows; delete duplicates. +

+
+
+

03

+

MCP projection

+

+ Project capabilities through one primitive factory. +

+
+
+

04

+

Runtime hosts

+

+ Refactor Node and Worker independently around their real + lifetimes. +

+
+
+

05

+

Parity proof

+

+ Conformance matrix plus runtime-native observation. +

+
+
+
+ +
+

+ Decision record and current guidance +

+
+
+

Repository decisions

+
    +
  • + #865 architecture synthesis +
    • +
  • + #866 accepted portfolio +
    • +
  • + #937 current-checkout review routing +
    • +
+
+
+

Primary external guidance

+
    +
  • + MCP TypeScript SDK server guide + — stateful/stateless deployment and host protection. +
    • +
  • + Cloudflare MCP handler guide + — stateless Worker handler as the current default. +
    • +
+
+
+

+ Method: current source inspection, deletion test, module depth, seam + reality, change leverage, locality, adapter parity, live issue state, + and current primary SDK/runtime guidance. No source or repository file + was changed. +

+
+
+ + + +

issue.title: architecture: adopt a deep operations kernel with independent runtime hosts
issue.body:
## Decision to review

Adopt **one deep runtime-neutral application spine with three honest runtime hosts**:

- deepen `@hevy-mcp/operations` into the application kernel shared by MCP and CLI callers;
- keep `@hevy-mcp/core` as the MCP projection of those operations;
- keep Node stdio, stateful Node HTTP, and stateless Cloudflare Worker HTTP/OAuth as independent concrete adapters;
- share safe semantic observations, while leaving exporters and lifecycle behavior in the runtime adapters;
- do **not** introduce a universal Node/Worker base class.

This issue owns the cross-runtime architecture decision and its invariants. It does not replace the implementation issues already accepted in the roadmap.

## Review baseline

Repository snapshot: `origin/main` at `2443cad60f74c21ec38592d2083e7fac1398401a` on 2026-08-07.

The current macro-shape is sound, but the application seam is still shallow:

- `packages/operations` has about 131 production lines and shares only `workouts.list`;
- Core has roughly 5,978 production lines and still contains 13 direct `runtime.getClient()` call sites versus one `runtime.getOperations()` call;
- execution scoping relies on a hand-maintained client option-index table and proxy;
- Node has rich tool, cache, client, and telemetry observation wiring, while the Worker does not yet project the same safe semantic events;
- Node HTTP sessions and isolated Worker requests have materially different state and lifecycle semantics.

## Target ownership

| Module | Owns | Must not own |
|---|---|---|
| `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | upstream HTTP mechanics, curated generated-client edge, endpoint identity, retry/request phases | MCP presentation, CLI rendering, runtime lifecycle |
| `@hevy-mcp/operations` | Hevy intents, pagination/search/composites, mutation safety, normalized outcomes, safe semantic observations | MCP schemas, process signals, Cloudflare bindings |
| `@hevy-mcp/core` | MCP tools/prompts/resources, response contracts, tool execution and protocol projection | Node process lifecycle, Worker auth/routing |
| `hevy-mcp` Node adapter | stdio, stateful HTTP sessions, shutdown, process/update lifecycle, Node exporters | Worker request semantics |
| `@hevy-mcp/worker` | request admission, bearer/OAuth routing, origin/CORS, request isolation, Cloudflare bindings/export | Node session/process abstractions |
| CLI adapter | argument parsing and human/JSON rendering | duplicate Hevy-domain workflows |

Dependency direction remains runtime-neutral: client mechanics feed operations, operations feed Core, and CLI consumes operations directly. Node and Worker compose Core independently.

## Runtime composition

### Node stdio

One process-scoped host composes a credential-scoped client, operations kernel, MCP projection, stdio transport, process lifecycle, and Node observation exporters.

### Node HTTP

One process host owns the HTTP listener and shutdown. Each stateful MCP session owns its server/transport and credential-scoped operation graph. Session security and cleanup stay concrete.

### Cloudflare Worker

Each admitted request remains isolated: authenticate, create a credential-scoped client/operations/Core graph, connect a stateless transport, respond, and dispose. Do not cache credential validation or mutable server state without the benchmark, revocation, and tenant-isolation evidence required by #879.

## Required invariants

- Adding a domain operation should not require a new execution-proxy index plus independent Core and CLI workflow implementations.
- Operation inputs and outcomes are concrete and typed; avoid a stringly `execute(capabilityId, unknown)` dispatcher.
- Expected absence, retryability, safe diagnostics, and metric identity remain distinct endpoint-policy facts. Unknown endpoints fail closed.
- Generated Kubb internals remain private behind curated Hevy client exports.
- Safe semantic observation is runtime-neutral; Sentry/OpenTelemetry/Cloudflare exporters remain adapter-specific.
- Node process/session state never leaks into the Worker, and Worker request isolation is not weakened for superficial reuse.
- MCP protocol compatibility is projected by Core and is not allowed to distort the application interface.
- No giant facade that merely mirrors every generated client method, and no capability megamanifest as a second source of truth.

## Migration route

Reuse the live roadmap instead of creating one large implementation branch:

1. Route the central endpoint-policy slice through #937 and coordinate its telemetry ownership with #928.
2. Deepen operations domain by domain in #872, starting with one end-to-end vertical slice.
3. Move explicit execution context and normalized outcomes with the operation slice; retire proxy-table entries only as callers migrate.
4. Keep public MCP contract work in #874 and the protocol-serving seam in #876.
5. Collapse duplicated Node lifecycle through #878 without merging stdio and HTTP transport implementations.
6. Add Worker semantic-observation parity and measure request admission through #879 before considering reuse.
7. Preserve the runtime contract matrix and isolation evidence in #880.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Maintainers mark this target architecture accepted, deferred, or rejected with rationale.
- [ ] The attached HTML review is commit-pinned and checksum-verified.
- [ ] A concrete operations interface is compared against at least two materially different designs before implementation.
- [ ] The first vertical slice has one owning implementation issue and explicit module ownership.
- [ ] Node stdio, Node HTTP, and Worker request lifecycles are covered by contract tests that preserve their different state models.
- [ ] Worker observation parity is measured semantically; runtime-specific exporter configuration is not forced into Core.
- [ ] Each implementation PR identifies its package/Changeset cascade from `repository/topology.json`.
- [ ] No implementation PR attempts to combine the full migration.

## Non-goals

- A universal runtime host or inheritance hierarchy.
- Combining stateful Node HTTP and stateless Worker transport code.
- Caching Worker credentials or mutable server state without evidence.
- Replacing curated, typed operations with a generic registry dispatcher.
- Duplicating #872, #874, #876, #878, #879, or #880.

## External constraints

The TypeScript SDK intentionally supports both stateful and stateless deployment modes: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/docs/server.md

Cloudflare recommends the stateless handler for new Worker servers: https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/model-context-protocol/apis/handler-api/

## Relationship to prior review

#937 remains the broader architecture-improvement tracker. This issue records the narrower Node/Cloudflare target architecture and routes its implementation through the existing roadmap.

issue.title: Apply one validation model to CI, artifacts, coverage, and releases
issue.body:
## Outcome

Local, pull-request, release, and deployment workflows consume one validation-lane model, test every public candidate artifact, and enforce honest coverage/release semantics without duplicated execution.

## Ownership seam

Safety-net consumers own workflow orchestration, reporters, credentials, artifact gates, coverage aggregation, and release/deployment policy. Stable lane facts come from the repository control plane.

## Scope

- Make aggregate lanes disjoint while retaining focused debug commands and intentional runtime diversity.
- Define and baseline the production coverage denominator; merge reports deterministically and add behavior-specific ratchets.
- Gate Node and CLI tarballs, Docker image, and Worker candidate artifacts before publication/deployment.
- Add structured release simulations for Node-only, CLI-only, Worker-only, mixed, release-PR, and publish cases.
- Separate deterministic artifact gates from retried live canaries with explicit health, rollback, and manual-override policy.
- Record execution count and wall-time before and after without weakening correctness.

## Non-goals

- Inventing a global coverage percentage before measuring the denominator.
- Making transient Hevy availability block package publication.
- Removing SHA pinning or security scans.
- Change-impact optimization before lane parity.

## Portfolio placement

Wave 4 — proof and enforcement

Primary priority: Maintainer leverage

## Dependencies

- [Repair generated-client output closure and enforce regeneration drift](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/870)
- [Centralize repository topology, artifact provenance, and validation lanes](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/873)
- [Generate the complete MCP contract matrix and conformance lane](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/880)

## Migration and release policy

Internal CI/workflow changes may break private composition. Preserve documented command aliases for one release cycle. Use an empty Changeset.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Local `test:pr`, pull-request CI, and release consume identical lane identities.
- [ ] Every public artifact is tested as the exact candidate that would ship.
- [ ] Coverage excludes/labels generated, type-only, and entrypoint files deliberately and enforces reviewed ratchets.
- [ ] Release simulations catch missing packages, wrong cascades, permissions/provenance errors, and failed canary/rollback paths.
- [ ] Duplicate builds/tests and Worker dry-runs are removed with measured savings.

## Validation

- `npm run test:pr`
- `npm run test:coverage`
- `npm run test:pack`
- `npm run test:pack:cli`
- `npm run worker:dry-run`
- `npm run check:release-candidates`
- `npm run check:package-changesets`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run check:types`
- `npm run check:changeset`

## Stopping conditions

- Do not lower existing gates to achieve disjointness.
- Stop if a live canary becomes the only proof that a deterministic candidate artifact is valid.

## Roadmap source

Portfolio decision: [Choose the improvement portfolio and breaking-change migration policy](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/866)

Architecture source: [Synthesize deep-module boundaries and cross-cutting opportunities](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/issues/865#issuecomment-5166093667)
